title: Align owner-session HTTP errors with accepted authorization and CSRF contract
requirements: Replace the private authorization response used by owner-session routes with the accepted 401 AUTH_REQUIRED error envelope, without revealing whether a login exists, a session expired, was revoked, or credentials changed.

For login, return 403 FORBIDDEN when Origin is missing or not in the exact runtime allowlist, 403 FORBIDDEN when X-Requested-With: crm is missing or wrong, and 415 UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE for a non-JSON Content-Type. Preserve stable malformed-payload behavior without disclosing authentication state.

For sign-out, distinguish an invalid or absent session (401 AUTH_REQUIRED) from an active session with missing/mismatched CSRF token (403 CSRF_FAILED) and from an untrusted Origin (403 FORBIDDEN). Do not revoke or disclose data in any rejected case.

Preserve all existing AUTH-001 fail-closed runtime, cookie, password, token-digest, origin matching, rate-limit and server-side session semantics. Do not add CORS, credentials, runtime configuration, bootstrap behavior or unrelated commands.
Add direct API and disposable-PostgreSQL integration assertions for each error code/status and each rejected sign-out must leave the session usable unless a valid sign-out is accepted.
acceptance: Owner-session responses follow the accepted docs/api.md authorization, CSRF and media-type error codes without an implementation-specific authorization code.
A rejected Origin, media type or CSRF request cannot create or revoke a session, and invalid credentials remain indistinguishable.
Focused API/integration tests, scope and whitespace checks pass.

shared_paths_approval.reason: Lead review found a direct mismatch between AUTH-001 route errors and the accepted admin authorization/CSRF/media-type contract; this repair changes only those observable error semantics and their evidence.
